findings.text: The old code escaped every ESC byte to ``. The new code only strips complete `ESC[...m` sequences, so any other ESC byte now goes into the XML raw. For example, a cursor sequence like `ESC[2K` or `ESC[1A`, or a bare ESC, is still emitted. ESC (0x1B) is illegal in XML 1.0, so JUnit parsers will reject the whole report.
The regex requires `[0-9;]+`, so a bare reset `ESC[m` (no digits) does not match and is left unstripped. The raw ESC then stays in the output and makes the XML invalid.
